correctness.rationale: For every even d>=4 over C, individual plane sections are smooth because their equations are Fermat-type of degree d. The pairwise plane-intersection lines fall into the four exhaustive support patterns of counts 6,4d^2,12d,3d^2 and multiplicities d+2,3,2,2. On each line the Fermat equation restricts to a*s^d+b*t^d for positive a,b, hence intersects in d simple points. Any rank-three arrangement point has all nonzero coordinate d-th powers equal and does not lie on the Fermat surface in characteristic zero. The local curve branches are therefore smooth with distinct tangent directions. The local delta formula, genus and count follow by exact integer identities and adjunction. The actual packaged check_reflection_divisor.py was run and returned REFLECTION_DIVISOR_VERIFY_OK; its d=4 calculation is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new object is the reduced divisor cut on each even-degree Fermat surface by all monomial reflection mirrors. The inspected initiating article counts 28 quasi-Galois centers for the quartic, while the later, stronger reflection paper classifies all centers for general degree; neither inspected full text computes the complete ordinary multiple-point basket on the surface, its delta invariant or its arithmetic genus. Classical ambient intersection flats are acknowledged and not claimed as new. Full claim-to-prior implication checks and published-finding queries identified no covering statement. Remaining risk is a previously tabulated, differently framed arrangement restriction.
residual_risks: A preexisting equivalent tabulation in older reflection-arrangement or Fermat-surface literature could remain undiscovered; a failed search is not novelty proof.
The 2025 Fermat-type arrangement article and 2022 plane-curve arrangements paper were not fully inspected, though their stated objects and accessible passages differ.

The result is a systematic specialization of established arrangement theory and may be viewed as implicit in that theory; the checked sources do not explicitly supply its surface transversality and basket.

value.rationale: This is the complete singularity classification of a natural geometric divisor: the union of fixed curves of the monomial reflection automorphisms on even-degree Fermat surfaces. The quartic case is canonical because the 28 planes are exactly those associated with all quasi-Galois centers, and it yields 664 distinct singular points with nontrivial high multiplicities. Uniform formulas for three strata, delta-invariant, normalization and arithmetic genus across infinitely many degrees give global intersection data relevant to log pairs and equivariant surface geometry. The claim goes beyond enumerating known reflection hyperplanes or routine numerical substitution.
